HO00004641.title: DocHouse: The Battle Of Chile Part 1
HO00004641.description:
A rare chance to see all three parts of Patricio Guzmàn's The Battle of Chile, an epic chronicle of the tumultuous events of 1973, resulting in the coup against Salvador Allende by Pinochet's army.

Part 1: The Insurrection of the Bourgeoisie examines the escalation of rightist opposition following the left’s unexpected victory in Congressional elections held in March 1973. Finding that parliamentary democracy would not stop Allende’s socialist policies, the right wing shifted its tactics from the polls to the streets. The film follows months of activity as a variety of increasingly violent tactics are used by the right to weaken the government and provoke a crisis.

HO00004642.title: DocHouse: The Battle Of Chile Part 2
HO00004642.description:
A rare chance to see all three parts of Patricio Guzmàn's The Battle of Chile, an epic chronicle of the tumultuous events of 1973, resulting in the coup against Salvador Allende by Pinochet's army.

Part 2: The Coup D’Etat opens with the attempted military coup of June 29, 1973, which is put down by troops loyal to the government. It serves as a useful dry run, however, for the final showdown, which everyone now realizes is only a matter of time. The film shows a left divided over strategy, while the right methodically lays the groundwork for the military seizure of power. The film’s dramatic concluding sequence documents the actual coup d’etat, including Allende’s last radio messages to the people of Chile, footage of the military assault on the presidential palace, and that evening’s televised presentation of the new military junta.

HO00004643.title: DocHouse: The Battle Of Chile Part 3
HO00004643.description:
A rare chance to see all three parts of Patricio Guzmàn's The Battle of Chile, an epic chronicle of the tumultuous events of 1973, resulting in the coup against Salvador Allende by Pinochet's army.

Part 3: The Power of the People deals with the creation by ordinary workers and peasants of thousands of local groups of “popular power” to distribute food, occupy, guard and run factories and farms, oppose black-market profiteering, and link together neighborhood social service organizations, first as a defense against strikes and lock-outs by factory owners, tradesmen and professional bodies opposed to the Allende government, and then increasingly as soviet-type bodies demanding more resolute action by the government against the right.

HO00007352.title: DocHouse: Boorman and the Devil

HO00007356.title: DocHouse: Christine Choy: Double Bill

HO00007357.title: DocHouse: Christine Choy: Mississippi Triangle
HO00007357.description: An intimate portrait of the Mississippi Delta, where Chinese, African American and white locals live in a complex world of cotton, labour and racial conflict.

HO00007408.title: DocHouse: Derek Vs Derek
HO00007408.description:
What do you do when your neighbour goes completely wild?
Award-winning director James Dawson’s new documentary is set in the rolling hills of Devon, telling the story of two neighbouring farmers who share the same name but take radically different approaches to land use. 

In equal parts hilarious and moving, the film shines a light on the vital debate surrounding the future of rural Britain, encouraging conversation around how farming and nature restoration might work together.

HO00007323.title: DocHouse: How Deep is Your Love
HO00007323.description:
With mesmerising underwater cinematography, HOW DEEP IS YOUR LOVE takes us way down below the surface with a team of scientists exploring the unknown: the deep sea, where 70% of our planet lies hidden.

Their life's work is finding, describing and naming strange and wonderful deep sea creatures, and now they find themselves racing against the looming threat of deep-sea mining, as they search for thriving ecosystems in the unexplored darkness.

Director Eleanor Mortimer weaves wonder with urgency, challenging us to balance the drive for resources with the intrinsic value of an ecosystem. As we journey through this breathtaking realm, we are left to ponder – how deep is our love?

HO00007346.title: DocHouse: Kikuyu Land
HO00007346.description:
While investigating Kenya's global tea industry, Nairobi journalist Bea Wangondu stumbles upon her own family's concealed secrets, pushing her to peel back the layers of Kenya's colonial legacy.

When the British colonised Kenya, they took control of prime tea-growing land, stripping Kikuyu people of Central Kenya of their lands and cultural identity. The plantations are still owned by some of the world's biggest corporations, supplying the global market, with local Kenyan's left to labour under abusive conditions on their own ancestral soil. 

As Bea follows a local man's legal challenge to retrieve his family's stolen land, she discovers a murky world of hidden evidence and untold wounds. Set against the beautifully captured richness of the landscape, KIKUYU LAND is a poetic, stunningly cinematic dive into a complex history.

HO00007410.title: DocHouse: Memorial / Liquidation
HO00007410.description:
In December 2021, Russia's Supreme Court ordered the liquidation of Memorial, the country's oldest human rights organisation, founded in 1987 to document and expose Stalinist terror. Ten months later, Memorial was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.
Taisiya Krugovykh and Vasily Bogatov filmed the process from the inside. We see the court hearings and repression against the supporters of Memorial, the evacuation of the organisation's archive before its Moscow office is seized, and the trial of its co-chair Oleg Orlov on charges of "discrediting the Russian Armed Forces," which ends with his imprisonment.

Shot in the tradition of direct cinema, without commentary or voiceover, the film traces the dismantling of Russian civil society through the people who lived it. Both filmmakers have been in exile in France since 2022.

HO00007341.title: DocHouse: Remake
HO00007341.description: In REMAKE, filmmaker Ross McElwee turns his lens on the passage of time and the uneasy space between documenting life and understanding it. The film traces McElwee’s relationship with his son Adrian, and the fragile bond the camera created between them while Adrian was alive, and now that he’s gone. Drawing from decades of footage, some shot by Ross, some by Adrian, the film becomes a layered excavation of memory and image making. Threaded through is the ghost of another project: a stalled effort by Hollywood to fictionalize McElwee’s 1986 classic, SHERMAN’S MARCH. What emerges is a work shaped by absence and propelled forward by a father’s love for his son.

HO00007339.title: DocHouse: Sherman's March
HO00007339.description:
Armed with a 16mm camera and a grant to make a documentary about the aftermath of William Tecumseh Sherman’s 1864 march to the sea, Ross McElwee gets sidetracked. After his girlfriend breaks up with him, Ross shifts his attention from the historical to the personal, to the battlefield of modern love, and embarks on a sociological chronicle that documents the courting rites and rituals of the New South.
A generous and humanistic portrait of several remarkable women that Ross meets along the way, SHERMAN’S MARCH is a landmark of first-person filmmaking that presaged everything from Michael Moore to reality TV. Now restored in beautiful 4k.

HO00007407.title: DocHouse: Steel on Film
HO00007407.description:
A journey through 50 years of Britain’s steel communities.
This event pairs Joe Cornick's impressionistic 16mm portrait of the final years of traditional steelmaking in Port Talbot, STEEL: THE BLOOD OF US (2026), with THE FACE OF CHANGE (1976),  Malcolm Hignett's documentation of the British Steel industry as it grappled with the seismic effects of recession and modernisation.
Made exactly 50 years apart, the two films offer contrasting perspectives on Britain's steel industry and the communities shaped by it.

HO00007347.title: DocHouse: The Attempted Murder of Salman Rushdie
HO00007347.description:
KNIFE explores renowned author Salman Rushdie’s life, career and recovery following a harrowing attempt on his life in 2022. The film includes never-before-seen footage shot by Rushdie’s wife, the American poet, novelist and visual artist Rachel Eliza Griffiths, in the time following the attack offering a graphic, unflinching, and deeply intimate account of his remarkable recovery and optimism for the future. Directed by Academy Award-winning director Alex Gibney, KNIFE is inspired by Rushdie’s bestselling memoir ‘Knife: Meditations After an Attempted Murder.’
Special preview screenings on 30 September with theatrically exclusive recorded Q&A with Alex Gibney, Salman Rushdie and Rachel Eliza Griffiths

HO00007322.title: DocHouse: The Cycle Of Love
HO00007322.description:
In 1977, PK, a young street artist from Delhi, picked up a handful of paintbrushes and a second-hand bicycle and set off on a 6000-mile journey to find the woman who had captured his heart.

Growing up poor and 'untouchable', young PK had to reckon with the caste system and with his own sense of self-worth, as he met fellow travellers and locals from all walks of life on his journey across the world. Oscar-nominated director Orlando von Einsiedel retraces PK's journey from India to Sweden in an extraordinarily uplifting film, that is not just about what can happen when you follow your heart, but is also a paean to the joy of chance encounters and the kindness of strangers.

HO00007358.title: DocHouse: The Disciple
HO00007358.description:
An outsider fueled by relentless determination works his way into the inner circle of the Wu-Tang Clan, where his ambition and creativity converge in the making of an album poised to ignite global controversy.

Wu-Tang Clan’s seventh studio album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin, was recorded in secret over six years, sealed in an ornate silver case, and first sold at a 2015 auction for a reported $2 million, under terms barring any commercial release until 2103. 

In THE DISCIPLE, director Joanna Natasegara tells the story of the album's unlikely origins and controversial reception, meeting Tarik Azzougharh - the Dutch-Moroccan superfan who talked his way into Wu-Tang Clan's inner circle and became the driving force of the now legendary album, Once Upon a Time in Shaolin.

HO00007406.title: DocHouse: The Eyes of Ghana
HO00007406.description:
A true love letter to cinema, THE EYES OF GHANA follows 93-year-old cameraman Chris Hesse, as he races against time to rescue a secret trove of film reels that uniquely captured the birth of African independence. 
Back in the 1950s and 1960s, Hesse was the personal cameraman to Ghana’s revolutionary leader Kwame Nkrumah. Always at Nkrumah's side and always filming, Hesse was witness to Africa’s tumultuous liberation movement. In 1966, Nkrumah was deposed in a coup and his rivals sought to destroy all the filmed records of his leadership, but Hesse found a way to preserve over 1000 reels.

Now in his 90s, Hesse is no less spirited and no less determined to pass on this celluloid legacy. He joins forces with filmmaker Anita Afonu to bring these barely seen reels to an audience in Accra, finally projecting a Ghanian perspective on their history. 

Filled with joy, verve and a dedicated focus on the importance of self-representation, THE EYES OF GHANA is a voyage through Ghanian cinema and a portrait of the country, from cinema’s inception through to the present day.

HO00007359.title: DocHouse: The Last First: Winter K2
HO00007359.description:
Director Amir Bar-Lev tells a complex, harrowing and moving story that takes an unflinching look at the industry of extreme mountain climbing and its changing culture.

Focusing on a 2021 expedition, this documentary follows Icelander John Snorri Sigurjónsson and the Pakistani father-son team of Ali and Sajid Sadpara, a party of mountaineers who set out to be the first to summit K2 in the winter, when the mountain’s conditions are the cruelest. The men soon find themselves sharing the treacherous ascent with influencer climbers and their film crews, commercial expedition clients, and a Nepalese team no longer content to help Westerners achieve mountaineering glory.

THE LAST FIRST: WINTER K2 takes us to the icy heights and unpredictable weather of K2 and reveals a surprising and layered story - one of strategy and determination, class and caste, money and power - all under life-and-death circumstances.

HO00007338.title: DocHouse: The Watergate Caper
HO00007338.description:
This archival documentary traces the rise and fall of Nixon from the presidential primaries of 1968 through the Watergate break-in of June 1972 to his resignation two years later, killing trust in the political process and the American presidency in the wake of the Vietnam War.
 The film draws on hundreds of hours of TV news taped off-air by the Nixon White House to tell the untold story of the Watergate burglars. How did tapping the wrong phone with a bug that didn't work lead to their arrests and Nixon's resignation? It also explores representations of the Nixon years in popular culture, using the music, commercials, and cinema of the era to evoke a fevered political landscape of culture wars, dirty tricks, paranoia and assassination. Sound familiar?

HO00007266.title: DocHouse: What We Were and What We Are
HO00007266.description:
First-time directors from the Sahrawi Refugee camps explore how their culture has changed after 50 years of enforced displacement. World Premiere screening of films and a Q&A. Organised by IRSAAN, UCL and UAL

WHAT WE WERE AND WHAT WE ARE is an event centered on a World Premiere screening of documentary films made by first-time directors from the Sahrawi Refugee camps. The young filmmakers have made works about their elders and how the Sahrawi culture has changed after 50 years of enforced displacement. The event will also comprise of talks and opportunities for Q&A sessions with the filmmakers and members of IRSAAN a Sahrawi led health charity based in the camps.

HO00007351.title: DocHouse:All Rivers Spill Their Stories to the Sea
HO00007351.description:
When thousands of dead crabs wash ashore in aa small North East fishing town, fisherman Stan Rennie becomes the unlikeliest of activists, in a grassroots fight for answers and a future.

Stan has worked this stretch of coastline, where the river meets the sea, for over fifty years. So when a vast tide of poisoned crabs, lobster and shellfish washes onto the beach, and officials seem unable or unwilling to establish a cause,  Stan finds himself thrown into battle: the unlikely figurehead of the campaign to uncover the truth about the die-off. 

Directed by Teessider Jeanie Finlay, this is a wry, David and Goliath story about navigating through grief and finding power in community, rich with Stan's own brand of heart, determination and gallows humour.

HO00007389.title: Frida: The Girl Just Doesn't Go Away

The Girl Just Doesn’t Go Away! explores the transformation from artist to icon of
Mexican painter Frida Kahlo, one of the most recognized influencers of our time.
The many representations of her, beyond a single image have been appropriated
by diverse groups from Chicanx and Mexican identity, disability to queer
representation, just some of the diverse groups within which Frida Kahlo has
become an inescapable reference and symbol. An extraordinary and unique
phenomenon, Fridamania! Combines the iconic, mythic with an inexhaustible
consumer culture.
